title: What torsion-free and metric each buy
promptMarkdown: In under 200 words and without the notes open: explain the role played by each of the two conditions (torsion-free, metric) in the proof that the Levi-Civita connection is unique, and why neither condition alone determines a connection. Support the second claim with two examples on Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^n,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$: a connection that is metric but has non-zero torsion, and one that is torsion-free but not metric. State the connections explicitly and say in one line each why they have the claimed properties.
hintLadder: Any connection on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $\partial_XY+A(X,Y)$ for a tensor $A$. Which algebraic conditions on $A$ correspond to 'metric' and to 'torsion-free'?
In $\mathbb{R}^3$ the cross product is antisymmetric and $\langle X\times Y,Z\rangle$ is alternating in all three slots.

criteria.criterion: Identifies that metric compatibility supplies the three permuted identities and torsion-freeness lets ∇_Y X, ∇_Z X, ∇_Z Y be rewritten so that the unknown terms cancel in the Koszul formula (or an equivalent account).
A correct metric connection with torsion, e.g. ∂_X Y + X × Y on R³, with the one-line reasons (⟨X×Y,Z⟩ + ⟨Y,X×Z⟩ = 0; torsion 2X×Y).
